events.text_en: Ông Lục Tiết, who sat the Feather Kindling forty-one times, leads forty unkindled outer disciples of Phượng Minh down to the wet grass below Tử Trúc Lâm to grow the bamboo seed the phoenix eats; the palace grants the garden sixty years of rice.
The garden's grove flowers and dies in a month; the bamboo rats of Trúc Thử Nguyên eat the fallen seed, then Bích Lãng's rice.
As the grove flowers, Tất Mạn Thu flowers with it to heal the field hands the rats have bitten, and dies before summer; her disciple Ninh Trúc Thực lights a censer in the young clumps.
Úy Thương Điền cuts flood terraces below the bamboo; the garden takes in the Water-rooted children of the coast.
Trúc Thực Viên writes its lineage as Wood and Water.
